memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Anyone who strikes a person with a fatal blow is to be put to death." - Exodus 21:12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God's law now turns from servants to the value of human life itself. The message is stark and clear: to take a life is the gravest of wrongs, because every human being bears the image of God (Gen 9:6). This was not cold cruelty but the opposite — a fierce declaration that people are not disposable. In a world that shrugged at bloodshed, God stood up for the sacredness of every soul.

We may not live under Israel's civil courts, but the truth beneath this law never expires: human life is precious to God. That means the life of the unborn and the elderly, the stranger and the enemy, the successful and the struggling. None of us has the right to treat another person as worthless.

Jesus deepened this even further. He taught that murder begins in the heart, in anger and contempt (Matt 5:21-22). So the question is not only "Have I killed anyone?" but "Do I honour the God-given worth of every person I meet?" Where the world sees people as obstacles or numbers, followers of Christ are called to see image-bearers, loved by their Maker.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Whose life or worth have I quietly dismissed in my heart?
How can I better honour the sacredness God places on every person?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, every life is precious to You. Guard my heart from anger and contempt, and help me honour the worth You have stamped on every person I meet. Amen.
